question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #34: A distributed deep learning model serving endpoint experienced severe throughput degradation and GPU memory fragmentation in MLOps, Model Serving & Drift Monitoring. During sustained peak inference, memory utilization hit 98% with OOM aborts specifically during 'Feature Store Architecture (Feast, Hopsworks)' execution.

### Engineering Challenge:
What is the optimal MLOps and architectural resolution to eliminate OOMs and optimize serving throughput for 'Feature Store Architecture (Feast, Hopsworks)'?

options.text: Allocate a static contiguous GPU VRAM tensor buffer sized to maximum possible sequence length for every incoming request.
Implement dynamic batching with continuous paged KV-cache management (PagedAttention) and FP16/INT8 activation quantization.
Disable model pipelining and force all transformer attention heads onto host system RAM via CPU swap.
Retrain the model from scratch using a single linear feedforward layer to bypass attention.

answer_explanation: In MLOps, Model Serving & Drift Monitoring, static allocation for sequence generation creates massive memory fragmentation. Continuous paged KV-cache allocation (such as vLLM) partitions key-value memory into non-contiguous blocks, slashing memory waste and preventing OOMs while maximizing concurrent throughput.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option B. Rationale: In MLOps, Model Serving & Drift Monitoring, static allocation for sequence generation creates massive memory fragmentation. Continuous paged KV-cache allocation (such as vLLM) partitions key-value memory into non-contiguous blocks, slashing memory waste and preventing OOMs while maximizing concurrent throughput.
